messages.subject: memory management
parts:
I have a Shiny app running on shiny-server on an Ubuntu EC2 instance behind an Apache2 proxy.  The app uses the following function to download some .xls files from the internet:

x   <- read.csv(summary(xls2sep(path.expand(thsurl), method = "csv"))$description)

This is a modification of the read.xls command from the gdata package (modified because was having issues with write permissions on the server, but that's a different topic.)

Sometimes everything works fine, but sometimes I get the following error:

Cannot popen '/usr/bin/which 'perl' 2>/dev/null', probable reason 'Cannot allocate memory'

If I run the same code in R on the Ubuntu server - or locally on my laptop - I never get this kind of error.  Do you know what might be causing this?  Do I need to increase the memory limits on shiny-server?  Or on the EC2 instance?

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: memory management
parts:
Does it happen only after you've run it a number of times? If so, it may be that your code is using memory and not freeing it up, due to references to old unused objects.

Also, what kind of instance are you running on? The micro instances only have about 600MB of memory, and typically aren't configured to use virtual memory (which would be costly and slow on EBS).

-Winston
